basis: Pinned function bodies, actual installed callable RTTI, bounded Capstone and scoped Ghidra C/highPcode review
facts: Both current auth request families inherit the pinned materializer.
The materializer calls the completion installer with the original request object.
The installer copies success/failure callable holders into the exact closure whose operator is the pinned HTTP completion.
The completion copies HttpResponse response-data begin/end bytes into a string and constructs one JsonCpp value.
The content-type header value is split at semicolon and compared with application/x-zstd.
For a nonempty non-zstd payload the reader writes its parsed document directly into that value.
Success and failure callable invocation pass that same value by reference, with no child/member wrapper selected between parsing and invocation.
The pinned nonce and token consumers read their existing fields from the delivered value.
limits: The compressed application/x-zstd path is not implemented or claimed by the candidate encoder.
This proves the plain JSON document shape, not complete sign-in success fields, token format, native startup, transport interception or successful login.
The older 1432-byte returned-string callback candidate is a different callable family and is not used in this proof.
No raw code, source coordinates, account/player values or credentials are published.
